s wife and daughter were in the room, but [**Name (NI) 234**] asked if she could
   meet alone. She discussed in more detail her concerns about her family
   member
s well-being, with the priority being her sis because of her

the center of her world.

s wife, who is a
   holocaust survivor, has been always been limited emotionally
She has

 In addition, she does not like her youngest

   [**Known lastname 232**] has to show her what door to enter. There was a discussion of

   uncertainty of Mr. [**Known lastname 232**]
s health. [**Known lastname 234**] will be returning to [**Location (un) 242**] for
   the weekend but will return, most likely on Tuesday, as she is meeting
   Wednesday with a lawyer to assess her family
s needs.
   Assessment:Assessment: The patient is being discharged with a primary diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction. No further cardiac work‑up is required at this time.
   Ms. [**Known lastname 232**] seems to have a very clear understanding of her family
   circumstances and has been working on future placement, such as
   visiting local nursing facilities. She has tried to work with the CP
   Foundation but found them to not be at all helpful. At times during the
   interview, she would start crying, most likely in response to her
   father
s illness and how overwhelmed she is feeling being the primary
   caretaker. Ms. [**Known lastname 232**] was assured that this writer and the SW on 11R
   would work together to assist her re disposition plans.
   Plans:
   1.       To inquire about possible placement options for the eldest
   daughter.
   2.       [**Known lastname 234**] was encouraged to speak with her father about her
   becoming his HCP versus his wife, who currently has that
   responsibility. She was given a copy of a HCP form to complete.
